subject: Request: Dedicated pool throughput carveout for nightly batch window
messages:
From: Samir Kothari <samir.k@stardrive.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@stardrive.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 May 2028 22:05:00 -0700
Subject: Nightly batch window - request for dedicated throughput guarantee

Hi Diego,

Thanks for the earlier call. We're in the final stages of committing to Redwood Dedicated for Stardrive's inference pipelines. One outstanding item for legal/procurement: our nightly ETL + generation window runs from 02:00-04:00 UTC and during that two‑hour slice we need sustained throughput for long sequences (avg 1.6k tokens/req). Historically we've seen preemption and queueing outside the window that increases tail latency for the batch jobs and blows up run times.

Ask: can Redwood provide a carveout in the Dedicated SLA that guarantees N sustained inference tokens/sec for the 02:00-04:00 UTC window (we're requesting 18k tokens/sec aggregate across our reserved pool), or alternatively provide a deterministic time-sliced reservation so our batch jobs are not impacted by tenant isolation? If neither is possible we need a clear crediting model tied to missed throughput for that window.

I've attached a spreadsheet with our hourly token profile and the PO/contract reference. Procurement wants written language to sign off.

Attachments: stardrive_batch_requirements.xlsx (hourly profile + PO)

Can you loop the right folks and let us know feasible options + timelines?

Appreciate it,
Samir
VP Engineering
Stardrive AI
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Kothari <samir.k@stardrive.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 May 2028 23:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightly batch window - request for dedicated throughput guarantee

Hi Samir — thanks for the spreadsheet, that helps. Tagging Lauren, Marissa and Aditya to align legal/pricing and infra constraints.

Short answer: we can offer a limited, contractual carveout but need to scope it precisely: Dedicated pools are designed for tenant isolation and predictable throughput, but there are two orthogonal constraints here — (1) concurrent burst behavior across tenants causing queueing at the scheduler level and (2) warm vs cold KV/cache state for long sequences which affects throughput.

Operational mitigations we can propose immediately while legal reviews contract language:
- Time-sliced reservations (reserve the pool exclusively for your tenant for the 02:00-04:00 window)
- Priority queueing for your pool during that window (reduces inter-tenant preemption but not absolute exclusivity)
- Pre-warm KV cache and preflight compilation for common long-sequence paths (reduces cold-start tail latency)

To move forward I need the following from you:
1) Confirm the aggregate tokens/sec target (sheet shows 18k tokens/sec; confirm if that is your hard requirement or a target).
2) Expected variability (p50/p95/p99 of tokens/sec during the window).
3) Whether you can accept a time-sliced reservation (we'll map it to a higher monthly committed capacity).

I'll draft two contract options and loop legal — Lauren / Marissa, can we get an initial review on a time-slice addendum vs a throughput-credit model? Aditya — rough infra note: time-slice is easiest to guarantee, credits are feasible but require instrumentation work for per-window telemetry and post-facto crediting.

— Diego
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightly batch window - request for dedicated throughput guarantee

Diego / team — quick internal on approach. Procurement will want clear, auditable guarantees or a simple crediting mechanism. Legal will push back on absolute language; we should offer both: a) a time-sliced reservation addendum (preferred, easier to operationalize), and b) a throughput SLA with monthly credits capped at X% of monthly committed spend (fallback).

Proposed commercial structure to present to Samir:
- Option A (Time‑slice guarantee): Reserve the pool exclusively 02:00-04:00 UTC. Price uplift: +18% on committed monthly list for reserved SKU to cover scheduling overhead and opportunity cost. SLA: 99.8% availability of reserved capacity during the window; missed availability triggers credits equal to 1.5x pro-rated hourly commit (capped).
- Option B (Throughput SLA + credits): No exclusivity; guaranteed minimum aggregated throughput of 12k tokens/sec during the window with telemetry. Missed throughput has a crediting formula tied to token‑seconds shortfall (requires instrumentation).

Marissa — can you draft the addendum language (simple: reserved window + uptime/credit clause) and attach to the proposal? Aditya — please confirm feasibility on instrumentation for Option B and expected lead time.

I'll prepare the commercial options for Samir and include the draft addendum (PDF).

— Lauren
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Kothari <samir.k@stardrive.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@stardrive.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightly batch window - request for dedicated throughput guarantee

Hi Samir — looping back with two concrete options. I've pasted the highlights below and attached a short draft addendum and the spreadsheet we received. Please reply with which option you prefer and any contract edits; procurement can use the same DocuSign link once you confirm.

=== Option A: Time-sliced reservation (recommended) ===
- Exclusive reservation of your dedicated pool 02:00-04:00 UTC daily
- Committed uplift: +18% on monthly reserved fee (one line item)
- SLA: 99.8% availability of reserved capacity during the window; credits = 1.5x pro-rated hourly reserve for missed minutes (max cap 10% of monthly fee)
- Operational: Redwood will pre-warm common KV paths and provide an operations runbook for your SREs to trigger preflight compilations.

=== Option B: Throughput SLA + credits (instrumentation required) ===
- No exclusivity; Redwood guarantees minimum 12k tokens/sec aggregate during 02:00-04:00 UTC
- SLA measurement: per-minute telemetry against agreed token counters; missed throughput triggers credits calculated from shortfall token‑seconds.
- Note: Option B requires 2-4 weeks to enable telemetry and validate counters before going live.

Next steps: pick A or B. If A, we'll issue a PO amendment and DocuSign package (link included). If B, we'll schedule a 2‑week instrumentation sprint and pilot.

Attachments: proposed_sla_addendum_draft.pdf, stardrive_batch_requirements.xlsx
DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/SD-2028-045

On Mon, May 13, 2028 at 22:05, Samir Kothari <samir.k@stardrive.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for the earlier call... [trimmed for thread]

Best,
Diego
From: Samir Kothari <samir.k@stardrive.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@stardrive.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightly batch window - request for dedicated throughput guarantee

Diego / team — thanks for the quick turnaround. We reviewed both options with our SRE and procurement. We prefer Option A (time-sliced reservation) for the first 90 days so we can validate end-to-end performance and run our nightly pipelines without concern for tail queueing. A few minor asks: 

- Can the addendum call out the exact token/sec floor during the window (we propose 18k tokens/sec aggregate) and a rollback clause after 90 days if our observed average is <14k?
- We need a daily telemetry report (CSV export) showing per-minute availability and tokens/sec during the reserved window.
- Docs/ops runbook: add a short appendix describing pre-warm steps and who to contact (SRE on-call).

If you can bake those items into the addendum we can get procurement to sign and route the PO by EOD Friday. I've cc'd Procurement.

Samir
VP Engineering
Stardrive AI
